There's been a bit of fuss about the direction of the #GamerGate tag concerning unhealthy obsession with SJW drama vs Staying on Target with ethics. To me, and I suspect to many others, this seems.. silly. Clearly, the extremes are bad, the question more seems to be about where the lines are drawn.

I think that there is a completely different issue at play here. An interesting one for you sociologist/behavioral types. This is actually a sort of fascinating phenomenon to witness and how we handle it may determine how well #GamerGate floats in the future. Bear with me, I'll try to walk through this to keep it simple.

>First, understand that #GamerGate is a community. For better and worse, it simply is. It's a particularly diverse community at that, and for many people, it is their first experience with something like this.

>Second, and most importantly, there are people who, like in any community, just want to interact. Sometimes people just want to say hi, talk about things that interest them, some just want to fight, and sometimes people just want to shitpost or throw some random thoughts into the ether to see what comes out.

Depending on your level of interaction on Twitter, your mileage may vary concerning whether this is an issue.

The first thing to understand in tackling this is that this is perfectly normal behavior. In fact, it's actually healthy. I'd even argue that it should be encouraged to a point, as this is what will keep us alive through the next year or beyond.

On the other end of that coin, it's a legitimate concern that useful information can be lost in the noise. Hand in hand with diversity is reconciling the problem of people who want to be social with the community versus people who are mostly here to 'work', as it were.

As TotalBiscuit has stated, 140 is a terrible format for discussion. It's less that he's a prophet and more that he's hitting on something fundamental about expressing complex concepts in narrow space. What should be a reasonable and interesting conversation is chopped down to caricatures and arguing. So let's have less arguing and more discussion on this.

I'm going to propose a solution to start with. It may not be a great solution, I'm not married to it, but it's a start for maybe hammering out something better. (I can even update this post with other suggestions if they pop up).

>Ancillary Tags Similar to the KiA solution, we simply add #Social, #SJW or #Ethics tags to things that are strictly off-topic, predominately SJW/culture related, or srsbsns. Not a replacement, an amendment.

I'm arguing that losing 5 characters is a small price to pay to provide some peace of mind. This allows people to browse and post in the general tag, or just browse a subtag. In the social/behavioral sense, it draws out borders for people who clearly need some lines/space from each other. (Again, it's natural, familiarity breeds contempt)

Whether you like my proposed solution or not, one thing that is clear is that discussion of this needs to be siphoned off of Twitter. It won't happen there and the shitflinging will just get worse every time this topic comes up. Hell, this doesn't even need to be the containment thread for it, but at the very least get this shit off of Twitter, it will not facilitate a real solution.

Best of luck and I hope something good comes of this.

Hi everyone, my name is Hussein. I am a Biomedical Scientist with a big interest in Neurodegenerative diseases. I want to let people know about a website I’ve just set up called Neuropendium. Neuropendium is a website dedicated to providing short, easy to read and clear reports about the latest in neuroscience research,specifically Neurodegenerative disorders for the moment. Best of all, it’s absolutely free for everyone. You don't even have to give any identifying information.

Just go to our website, sign up with your email and every 2 weeks you’ll receive an email letting you know when new reports are out. Even that is optional though, you don't need to sign up to get access to the reports, just visit the reports section of the site. Right now my focus is on Alzheimer’s and Parkinson's research but I hope to expand to more diseases in the future.

Why am I doing this? Well I've always had a particular interest in Neuroscience and was eager to learn to about latest research that emerged in the field. After 4 years of ongoing study in the biomedical field I finally got to the point where I could easily read and understand the research papers that scientists write to describe their experiments into diseases such as these. I realised however that this shouldn't be a privilege afforded to those with the time, money and necessary background in science. For someone outside the field, keeping up to date with Neuroscience research is hard. Generally they have to rely on mainstream media where the research is often misinterpreted or exaggerated.

However the actual research papers are difficult to understand for non-scientists due to their length and use of scientific jargon as well as being difficult to access. Costly price restrictions are placed on research papers by publishers which only universities or large research groups can afford.These restrictions are especially unfair to the sufferers of these diseases, their friends and family. For these reasons I decided to set up Neuropendium.

Neuropendium is not meant to provide people with medical advice, that will always be the job of a doctor, but Neuropendium will help to keep people informed and educated about their conditions. In addition I think the site could be very useful to anyone else that is simply interested in these diseases. Undergraduate science students in particular may find the reports useful in their studies.

We also have plans to add more pages to the site which will be useful for students and people who want to get more details about how research is done in Neuroscience and in biomedical science in general.

So what do I need from you? Well honestly nothing. I'm just here to let you know that the site and it’s services are here and ready for your use if you need them! As I said it’s completely free and I do not intend to ever charge a fee for accessing the reports. If you’d like to support the site please just spread the word and give a like to our FB page or follow us on twitter! Also as this is very much a work in progress for me, any feedback on the design of the website, or the reports themselves would be much appreciated. Thanks!

How would stem cell research be able to lessen/eliminate NDD?

Well at the core of neurodegeneration is of course the death of neurons and other cells of the nervous system. Stem cells have the capability to differentiate or transform into many types of cells, including cells of the nervous system. As such if we can develop an efficient, safe and easy to reproduce method of generating neuronal cells from stem cells, we may be able able to replace cells that are damaged in neurodegeneration.

This is of course a simplified explanation and there are many hurdles and challenges to the use of stem cells to treat NDDs.
